subject.title: improve(ci): reduce Blacksmith registrations for pull requests

question: Does the measured reduction of roughly six Blacksmith registrations justify accepting the modest increase in per-shard serial work and hosted-runner variability for `security-fast`?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but the preferred balance between organization runner-registration headroom and PR feedback latency is an operational ownership choice that CI cannot determine permanently.

options.title: Accept measured consolidation
options.body: Merge the 14-job plan because the live run remained within recent wall-time variance while materially reducing Blacksmith registrations.

options.title: Relax to 16 jobs
options.body: Reduce consolidation if the final-head or follow-up runs show the slowest shard moving outside the established timing range.

recommendation.title: Accept measured consolidation
recommendation.body: Merge the 14-job plan because the live run remained within recent wall-time variance while materially reducing Blacksmith registrations.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository history shows the strongest ownership signal for CI shard balancing and critical-path tuning, and this contributor assembled the baseline and live measurements.
